submission.natural_language_explanation: Induction head: it is strong (about 0.5-0.9 of max) on the second or later occurrence of a rare word that splits into several sub-word tokens (an unusual name, place, acronym or code identifier such as Myrmecia, Sheppard, AMOC, Rhosbeirio, novatec). It fires on each piece of that word whose same token appeared earlier in the context followed by another piece, so the first and middle pieces are strong and the last piece is weak. Text with no earlier copy is near zero, as are first occurrences, single-token common words repeated (Paris, John: about 0.1) and earlier copies tokenised differently (sentence-initial 'Mississippi' vs ' Mississippi'); repeated common short phrases ('the big red car' twice) or repeated random token strings reach only about 0.25-0.4.

rival_explanations: Generic induction head: any token that repeats an earlier token, including single-token common names and words (Paris, John, the), is predicted equally strong, so a repeated common name would be active.

Rare-subword detector: middle pieces of rare, multi-token proper nouns fire whether or not the word appeared earlier, so first occurrences such as 'In Landewednack church' with no earlier copy would be active.
Copy-verification head: it fires only when the repeated sequence continues as it did before, so 'Myrmecia ... Myrmidon' (same prefix, new continuation) would be inactive.
